A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACE and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original appendices A–G match v2's B–H, with additional material identifiable separately. Minor layout defects do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-J and Qwen3-8B knowledge-editing evaluations, neuron interventions, layer ablations, and attribution analyses, including Tables 2–4 and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original prompt controls, AlphaEdit comparisons, counterfactual evaluations, general-benchmark results, and human validation of dataset labels.

M1.justification: The original attribution scores, query/value identification, and PMET-based editing procedure remain unchanged. Appendix J adds an ACE variant using AlphaEdit's null-space-constrained editing backbone, constituting a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates factual recall on filtered MQuAKE. v2 retains this coverage and adds evaluations on CSQA, BBH, MMLU, and GSM8k, plus counterfactual scenarios constructed by mismatching relation labels (Appendix L). These substantially broaden the evaluated tasks and editing conditions.

E2.justification: The original Base, FT, ROME, MEMIT, and PMET comparison is retained. Appendix J and Table 10 add AlphaEdit as an evaluated baseline on both GPT-J and Qwen3-8B, alongside the new ACE adaptation.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce zero-shot, one-shot, and nonoverlapping few-shot prompts; matched edited-layer budgets for ACE and baselines; and masking of final value edits. Appendix K adds overlap-rate evaluation using four human annotators and 80 sampled questions. These are additional evaluation designs; the original experiment settings and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's neuron and layer ablations, v2 adds prompt-dependence controls (Table 5), layer-budget sensitivity comparisons (Table 6), annotation validation (Table 11), attribution stability across sampling and prompts (Tables 13–15), intermediate-activation analysis after masking value edits (Tables 16–17), and counterfactual robustness tests. These address substantially more questions about ACE's mechanisms and reliability.

E5.justification: Appendix L.2 newly reports multiple inference runs and averaged layer-importance scores under Pass@1, Pass@2, Pass@3, and Pass@5 settings. The existing 1,000-trial neuron-ablation description is retained. No seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests are added, and an increase in runs for the original results is not established.

E6.justification: Original results remain unchanged, including ACE's 46.45/58.24 GPT-J/Qwen3 averages in Table 2. New results include ACE (AlphaEdit) at 49.24/61.54 versus AlphaEdit at 39.27/45.59 (Table 10), and counterfactual ACE averages of 43.58/54.27 (Table 18). Prompt, layer-budget, locality, annotation, attribution, and timing results are also added. These are additional variant or scenario results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 provides attribution definitions and editing optimization equations. v2 retains them and adds Appendix M's formal arguments about logit linearity, first-order log-probability attribution, importance additivity under negligible local curvature, and PMET update linearity. This introduces substantial theorem and proof content without changing the original attribution formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same query–value mechanism, attribution-guided editing contribution, and reported GPT-J/Qwen3 improvement claims. The additional experiments and backbone variant do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning reduced dependence on in-context examples, a value-only editing bottleneck, transfer to another editing backbone, attribution stability, preservation of unrelated capabilities, and propagation through implicit subjects (Sections 6.3 and 6.5; Appendices J and L). Appendix M also explicitly restricts importance additivity to a local first-order approximation.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly discloses four A800 GPUs with 80 GB each, knowledge-vector precomputation and caching, and separate precomputation and update timings. A new reproducibility statement reports code supplied in supplementary materials, whose availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. Existing hyperparameters and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the AlphaEdit citation by Fang et al. and positions ACE as compatible with that null-space editing approach. Section 2 and the existing detailed related-work discussion otherwise retain their citations and positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose, including the abstract, method, and conclusion, remains nearly verbatim. v2 adds experimental subsections and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements; expands and renumbers the appendix contents; and updates conference-header and contact information. The original narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation through Tables 5–6 and 10–19; Table 10 also redisplays Table 2 with additional rows. The six original figure images are unchanged, while several figures and tables move or are renumbered. Layout changes include an overlapping Section 4.2 heading and Takeaway 1 on v2 page 5.

improvement.justification: The prompt and matched-layer controls (Tables 5–6) address confounds that v1 did not isolate. The AlphaEdit and counterfactual evaluations broaden empirical support, while computational-cost disclosure improves transparency. These gains are tempered by preservation claims without unedited-model controls (Tables 12 and 19), and Appendix M.5's unsupported inference that linear PMET updates require additive attribution. The net quality gain is therefore useful but limited.
